title: Redis Streams
subtitle: XADD, XREAD, consumer groups, and durable messaging
author: KERNAL

whyItExists.problem: Pub/Sub messages are lost if no subscriber is connected. Lists don't track which messages have been processed. Distributed systems need durable, replayable event logs where multiple consumers can share work without double-processing.
whyItExists.solution: Redis Streams are an append-only log. Every message is persisted with a unique auto-generated ID. Consumer groups allow multiple workers to share a stream while ensuring each message is processed by exactly one worker. Unacknowledged messages can be recovered.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Event sourcing, durable job queues, activity feeds with history, microservice event buses, IoT event collection.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Simple fire-and-forget notifications (use Pub/Sub — simpler). Full-featured message brokers with complex routing (use Kafka or RabbitMQ).

explainModes.beginner: A Stream is like a conveyor belt that never forgets what passed on it. Every item gets a timestamp ID. Workers can grab items from wherever they left off, and the belt keeps a record of what was processed.
explainModes.simple: XADD appends a message with auto-generated ID. XREAD fetches new messages since a given ID. Consumer groups let multiple workers share a stream — each message goes to only one worker. XACK marks a message as done.
explainModes.standard: Redis Streams are ordered, immutable message logs. Each entry has a unique ID (timestamp-sequence) and multiple field-value pairs. Consumer groups track per-consumer delivery positions and maintain a Pending Entries List (PEL) of unacknowledged messages. XACK removes from PEL; XPENDING inspects it; XCLAIM reassigns stuck entries.
explainModes.technical: Stream entries are stored in a radix tree of listpack nodes, with each listpack holding sequential entries. The ID is a millisecond timestamp plus a sequence number, ensuring monotonic ordering across restarts. Consumer group state is stored in the stream's metadata. MAXLEN / MINID trims the stream to prevent unbounded growth. Streams survive restarts when persistence is enabled.
explainModes.deepDive: The Pending Entries List (PEL) is a rax tree mapping entry-id → {consumer, delivery-time, delivery-count}. XCLAIM atomically transfers an entry from one consumer to another when it exceeds an idle threshold. XAUTOCLAIM (Redis 6.2+) automates this by claiming all PEL entries idle for more than N milliseconds in a single command. The NOACK option in XREADGROUP skips PEL registration for high-throughput fire-and-forget in a group context.

content.text: Redis Streams are an append-only log of messages. Unlike Pub/Sub, messages are persisted. Unlike Lists, streams have unique IDs, support multiple consumers sharing work, and track which messages each consumer has acknowledged.

content.definition: A message in a Redis Stream, identified by a unique auto-generated ID (milliseconds-sequence, e.g. 1699100000000-0) and containing one or more field-value pairs.

content.code:
# Append an event (* = auto-generate ID)
XADD events * action "click" button "submit" userId "42"
# Returns: "1699100000000-0"  (timestamp-sequence ID)

# Append with explicit ID
XADD events 1699100001000-0 action "purchase" amount "99.99"

# Read all messages from the beginning
XRANGE events - +
# Returns: list of [id, [field, value, ...]]

# Read from a specific ID onwards
XRANGE events 1699100000000-0 +

# Read newest messages (blocking — waits up to 5 seconds)
XREAD COUNT 10 BLOCK 5000 STREAMS events $
# $ means "only new messages after now"

# Count entries
XLEN events

# Trim stream to last 1000 entries
XADD events MAXLEN ~ 1000 * action "view"

content.text: Consumer groups allow multiple workers to share a stream. Each message is delivered to exactly one consumer in the group. If a worker crashes without acknowledging, the message stays in the Pending Entries List (PEL) for recovery.

content.code:
# Create a consumer group starting from new messages ($)
XGROUP CREATE events workers $ MKSTREAM

# Worker 1 reads up to 5 messages
XREADGROUP GROUP workers consumer1 COUNT 5 STREAMS events >
# > means "give me messages not yet delivered to this group"

# Worker 2 reads next 5 messages
XREADGROUP GROUP workers consumer2 COUNT 5 STREAMS events >

# Acknowledge a processed message
XACK events workers 1699100000000-0

# Check pending (unacknowledged) messages
XPENDING events workers - + 10  # list up to 10 pending

# Claim a stuck message (idle for 60+ seconds)
XCLAIM events workers consumer2 60000 1699100000000-0

# Auto-claim all messages idle for 60+ seconds (Redis 6.2+)
XAUTOCLAIM events workers consumer2 60000 0-0 COUNT 10

content.text: Always trim streams with XADD MAXLEN ~ 1000 or a periodic XTRIM to prevent unbounded memory growth. The ~ allows approximate trimming which is much faster.

questions.question: What is the key difference between Redis Streams and Pub/Sub?
options: Streams persist messages; Pub/Sub messages are lost if no subscriber is connected
questions.explanation: Streams store messages in an append-only log that survives restarts (with persistence). Pub/Sub messages vanish if no subscriber is connected at the moment of publish.

questions.question: What does XACK do?
options: Adds a message to the stream
Marks a message as successfully processed, removing it from the Pending Entries List
questions.explanation: XACK removes a message from the consumer group's Pending Entries List (PEL). Without XACK, Redis considers the message still in-flight and it can be claimed by another consumer.

questions.question: What does the > symbol mean in XREADGROUP?
options: Read from the end of the stream
Read messages with IDs greater than a given ID
Read messages not yet delivered to any consumer in this group
questions.explanation: The > special ID in XREADGROUP means 'give me new messages that haven't been delivered to any consumer in my group yet'. Using a numeric ID instead reads from the consumer's pending list.

faq.q: How do I process failed messages (pending)?
faq.a: Use XPENDING to find unacknowledged messages and XCLAIM to reassign them to another consumer for reprocessing. XAUTOCLAIM (Redis 6.2+) automates this.
Yes unless you trim it. Use XADD MAXLEN ~ 1000 to cap at ~1000 entries, or run XTRIM periodically. The ~ prefix allows approximate trimming which is 10x faster.

faq.q: Can multiple groups read the same stream?
faq.a: Yes. Each consumer group maintains its own read position. Group A and Group B can both process every message independently, like separate queues reading from the same log.
